notes: Authored fields: domain, cluster, maturity, verified_on, triggers, related. Generated fields (description, body_lines, scripts, evidence_count) are overwritten by 'python tools/skillkit.py index --write'.

skills.name: chromium-crash-forensics
triggers: is it the browser or the extension
skills.description: Use when Chrome/Edge/Electron crashed, a tab died ("Aw, Snap!"), the whole browser restarted, or someone asks "is it the browser or the extension?". Reads Crashpad minidumps for the exception code (0xE0000008 = renderer out-of-memory), checks the profile exit_type, and classifies browser-vs-renderer-vs-extension crashes — including the fact that userscripts run *inside* the page renderer.

skills.name: codex-relay-model-triage
triggers: Model X is not available for this group
changed the model but it still fails
skills.description: Use when an OpenAI-compatible relay/proxy answers "Model X is not available for this group", 404 on /responses, or 403 "Insufficient account balance" — or when someone says "I changed the model but it still fails". Traces the effective model through the provider manager DB, the live client config and the per-conversation model, then verifies which model names the account's group actually offers.

skills.name: dsh-sandbox-workarounds
triggers: SSL connection could not be established
skills.description: Use when commands fail for environment reasons rather than logic reasons inside a confined agent sandbox — schannel SEC_E_NO_CREDENTIALS or "The SSL connection could not be established", CIM/WMI access denied, EPERM when spawning a child with piped stdio, UnicodeEncodeError from a GBK console, a long command that gets backgrounded, or `spawn ENOENT` for an executable that demonstrably exists (a missing working directory, or a Microsoft Store app execution alias).

skills.name: frontend-interaction-engineering
triggers: click does nothing after a drag
frame loop keeps running when idle
skills.description: Use when building or reviewing an interactive front-end component — canvas/WebGL scenes, drag-and-drop toys, physics piles, scroll or pointer effects, "make this feel right" tuning. Covers the rendering-path choice, gesture design and the click-vs-drag traps, physics patterns that read as natural (angle-of-repose piles, monotone restores, integer snapping), frame-loop hygiene, and how to verify feel objectively with counters and control experiments rather than screenshots.

skills.name: frontend-motion-audit
triggers: is this WebGL or an image
what interaction techniques does this site use
skills.description: Use before rewriting, optimizing or judging a deployed front-end — "is this WebGL or just an image?", "what library is this?", "why is this page heavy?", "what interaction techniques does this site use?". Audits already-downloaded artifacts offline: framework/library detection, real-time rendering vs static art, motion techniques, design tokens, responsive strategy, lazy chunks, and missing production concerns (reduced motion, CLS, social card).

skills.name: headless-cdp-toolkit
skills.description: Use when a page must be rendered to be understood — JS-only SPAs, "can you see this site?", interstitial/consent gates that need a click, screenshot comparison across viewports, or verifying a component after a change. Drives headless Chromium over the DevTools Protocol with zero npm dependencies (Node 22+ has global fetch and WebSocket).

skills.name: immersive-webgl-scene-patterns
skills.description: Use when building or reviewing an immersive hero/scene component — a WebGL black hole, particle field, shader-driven landing hero, or any "wow" interactive canvas. Covers the progressive-enhancement state machine, lazy scene loading with pre-warm, static-image fallback, pointer drag + keyboard parity, frame-rate-independent damping, frame-loop hygiene (delta clamp, visibility pause, context loss), DPR/responsive-FOV handling, and how to verify it headlessly.

skills.name: tampermonkey-store-forensics
triggers: recover userscripts after a profile move
skills.description: Use when you need the real source or settings of a userscript — to debug why it stops working, to review what it can access, or to recover scripts after a profile move. Tampermonkey keeps everything in a compressed LevelDB inside the browser profile, so grep/strings fail; this reads the LevelDB table format and Snappy by hand and extracts scripts, GM_setValue config and per-script metadata.
